key_insight: Mixing near no-slip stagnation points on solid surfaces follows universal Pe-dependent scalings, with a transition at t_B ~ Pe^(1/3) from stretch-dominated decay to boundary-controlled exponential mixing.
engineering_relevance: This provides a predictive scaling law for scalar transport in porous media and obstacle-laden flows, useful for designing mixers, reactors, and contaminant transport models.
method: Analyze thin solute blobs moving along separatrices ending at solid-boundary stagnation points.
Derive an analytical theory coupling advection, stretching, and diffusion near upstream stagnation points.
Validate the predicted asymptotic scalings against numerical simulations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a complete analytical theory that is explicitly validated by numerical simulations, with asymptotic laws confirmed for c_max(t) and blob width σ(t).
watch_item: The results are stated for thin blobs near generic single obstacles and may not directly transfer to complex geometries, multi-obstacle interactions, or flows without clear stagnation-point structure.
paper_title: Scalar mixing by stagnation points on solid surfaces
